body: ## What this adds The design note for **#6004** (wave-2 follow-up of the worlds programme #5955, parent topic #5973): what authority id should reserve to the server/world admin **from day one**, and what is genuinely delegable to a world community — argued from LambdaMOO's documented 1990–1996 governance arc (wizards → 1992 devolution → 1993 ballot system → Mr. Bungle → 1996 recentralization). New record: `doc/2026-11-08T12-50-00Z_design_id6004_lambdamoo_governance_arc/`, linked from `doc/README.md`. ## Contents - **§1 Reserved authority** — a table of what cannot be outvoted, each row tied to the surface that already exists in `pkgs/id` (BUILDER install path, capability ceilings, admin token, resource envelope, MODERATOR revoke, host serving policy), with the two invariants that follow: no governance body may widen its own authority, and every exercise of reserved authority is a logged entry referencing what it changed. - **§2 Delegable to the community** — content rules and parameters, reviewer sets, appeals, pre-approval of in-world submissions, moderation-pack adoption/parameterization, and quota policy within the envelope. Includes the Mr. Bungle lesson mapped to id's actual surface: attribution is reserved (per-user function mapping #5967), delegation is always a strict subset (DELEGATE/attenuation), presentation may change how a participant looks but never who they are or what they did, and a moderation library never acts *as* a participant. - **§3 Quota as a governance tool** — LambdaMOO's base allocation plus discretionarily granted increases judged on quality/utility, read as the missing per-principal building quota in id; grants are logged content decisions, never envelope changes, and never a punishment lever. - **§4 The reserved-authority checklist** — 18 numbered items in three groups (world admin / host operator / delegable) plus the three platform invariants nobody delegates. ## Scope Docs only, no code. The note supplies the authority split #5973's own deliverable must respect; it does not design the moderation-library interface, the pre-approval binding, or the quota data model (each named as a remaining decision in §5). Closes #6004. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Documentation** * Added a design note outlining governance decisions, audit and appeal expectations, and quota recommendations, with historical context and related open questions. * Added the note to the dated design-records index with a brief description and issue reference.
